claims.text: The proposed hybrid machine-learning model combines physics-based phonon-disorder descriptors with training data from first-principles lattice-dynamics calculations.
The hybrid model can predict low phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys more accurately than current empirical or ab initio approaches.
High-entropy alloys have chemically disordered, multicomponent structures.
Force-constant fluctuations and chemical disorder influence phonon dynamics in high-entropy alloys.
The model will be validated using in situ inelastic neutron or X-ray scattering data.
Local force-constant variations cause disorder-induced phonon scattering.
Disorder-induced scattering affects phonon attenuation, lifetimes, and dispersion.
Encoding chemical disorder and local bonding variations as quantitative descriptors allows the model to represent the relevant phonon-scattering physics.
Using these descriptors enables more precise prediction of effective phonon-scattering rates.
Enhanced phonon scattering and short phonon lifetimes are associated with reduced lattice thermal conductivity.
Alloys predicted to have low phonon thermal conductivity will exhibit short phonon lifetimes, dispersion anomalies, and enhanced attenuation.
The hybrid model will reduce prediction error by approximately 10–20% relative to previous empirical models.
Inelastic-scattering measurements will directly correlate with the model's predicted scattering rates.
Current empirical and ab initio methods lacking integrated disorder descriptors have larger prediction uncertainty than the proposed model.
The model is applicable primarily to high-entropy alloys having chemical-disorder levels and phase structures similar to those represented in its training set.
The model's accuracy may diminish for alloys with substantially different bonding characteristics.
The model's accuracy may diminish when unrepresented defect-induced scattering mechanisms dominate.
The magnitude of prediction improvement depends on alloy complexity and training-data quality.
